queries: WITH per_rating AS (SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate * 1.0 / rental_duration) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS film_count FROM film WHERE rental_duration >= 5 GROUP BY rating), bench AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS benchmark FROM per_rating WHERE avg_ratio IS NOT NULL) SELECT p.rating, p.avg_ratio, p.film_count, p.avg_ratio / b.benchmark AS ratio_to_benchmark FROM per_rating p CROSS JOIN bench b WHERE b.benchmark IS NOT NULL

assumptions.assumption: '5 days as the cutoff for a long rental period' is read inclusively: long rental means rental_duration >= 5 (5, 6 and 7 days).

Ratings with NULL avg_ratio are excluded from the benchmark. Ratings are kept in the output even if their own average is NULL. Since rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL, this does not happen in practice.
film_count counts all long-rental films in the rating group.

alternatives.interpretation: Long rental means strictly more than 5 days (rental_duration > 5, i.e. 6 and 7 days).

assumptions.assumption: '5 days as the cutoff for a long rental period' is read inclusively: long means rental_duration >= 5.
The benchmark is computed over the per-rating averages of the long-rental films only (the filtered set), not over all films. Ratings with a NULL average are ignored by AVG.
film_count counts all long-rental films in each rating, including any with NULL rental_rate.

assumptions.assumption: '5 days as the cutoff for a long rental period' is read as rental_duration >= 5 (5 days counts as long).
Ratings with NULL rating are not expected (verified 5 levels); the benchmark is the unweighted mean of per-rating averages over ratings present among the long-rental films.
film_count counts all long-rental films in the rating, including any with NULL ratio (none possible since rental_rate and rental_duration are NOT NULL).
